Transcript:
A robot entered an Alaska cloud. A model handed it nineteen million gallons.
On August twenty third, Rainmaker seeded clouds over the Kenai Peninsula.
Two Elijah drones made ten sorties in seven coordinated missions, releasing nineteen silver iodide flares.
The releases sat in Rainmaker's temperature band, totaling roughly three hundred seventy four grams.
Rainmaker manually tracked seven features in P A H G NEXRAD data.
The reflectivity was observed. Calling those features seeding signatures was the company's interpretation.
The analysis subtracted five D B Z as assumed background across twenty seven conversion relationships.
The company mean was fifty seven point six two acre feet, about nineteen million gallons.
Its spread was forty one point seven to eighty nine point three five acre feet, not total uncertainty.
The lowest radar beam sat roughly eighteen hundred to twenty two hundred meters above sea level.
The report provides no ground gauge or tracer confirmation at the surface.
Independent S N O W I E research tracked seeded plumes from radar to ground gauges.
Rainmaker says a saturated column made losses less likely, and seven repeated radar features are meaningful evidence.
Score it honestly. Alaska saw a robotics demonstration and a company modeled water total.
The drones delivered the flares. The model delivered the number. Next time, send a measuring cup.
